title: Peace & Conflict: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the foundational vocabulary for peace, war, justice and conflict resolution.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Peace & Conflict foundations — peace, war, pacifism, just war and reconciliation.
final_note: You now know the key terms for studying war and peace.

concepts.def: Absence of conflict — and presence of justice and harmony
Belief that all violence is wrong
War that meets strict moral conditions
Letting go of resentment for wrongs done

walkthroughs.body_html:
Jesus: 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God' (Matthew 5:9).

The Islamic greeting 'As-salamu alaykum' — 'Peace be upon you' — comes from the same root as Islam (submission, peace).

Both faiths see peace as more than the absence of war — it includes justice, harmony and right relationship with God.

Some Christians are pacifists — believing all violence is wrong.

The Quakers (Religious Society of Friends, founded 1652) are famous pacifists, refusing military service in both World Wars.

Key text: Jesus' 'turn the other cheek' (Matthew 5:39) and 'love your enemies' (Matthew 5:44).

After conflict, religion calls for reconciliation — restoring relationships.

Examples: Desmond Tutu's Truth and Reconciliation Commission in South Africa (1996) after apartheid.

Christian foundations: 'Be reconciled to your brother' (Matthew 5:24). Islamic teaching: pardoning is praised (Qur'an 42:40).
